0. Getting started

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-00-start.Rmd
book-00-start.Rmd

What you will learn

Install the client, choose a practice environment, and check both package versions.

This chapter creates the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Before you start

You need R 4.1 or newer (the recorded run used R 4.6.2), internet access for installation, and either an Opal with dsOMOP 2.10.4 or the local DSLite practice server below. RStudio is a convenient editor; ordinary R also works. Keep a copy of this book’s checkout: the helper scripts live in tools/book/.

Run this installation block once, before the examples. It installs every package used by the lessons, the offline server and the reproduction tools. Installation changes your library and is not executed during the book build. The two dsOMOP tags must be available on GitHub; this book’s recorded run used the matching locally tagged sources.

install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal", "DSLite", "DBI", "RSQLite",
                   "resourcer", "withr", "openssl", "jsonlite", "knitr",
                   "rmarkdown", "pkgdown", "bslib"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBase@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOP@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")

The client is the package on your computer. The server runs requests near the data; DSLite lets you run it locally for practice. Pandoc is also needed to rebuild the site (RStudio includes it). The reproduction notes record the dependency versions used for this book.

Check the client 

library(dsOMOPClient)
vapply(c("dsOMOPClient", "dsOMOP", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(package) as.character(packageVersion(package)), character(1))
#> dsOMOPClient       dsOMOP          DSI       DSLite dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.4"     "2.10.4"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"
ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"

This reports the package on your computer. A correct client version alone does not prove that the server has the matching methods.

Load two public synthetic datasets

The practice server has two resources. GiBleed supports the introductory schema and vocabulary lessons. Synthea27Nj supplies hemoglobin and other numeric measurements with units. Both contain fictional patients; “numeric” means populated numeric fields, not real patient records. GiBleed has 44,053 measurement rows but no populated value_as_number, so it cannot teach lab-value reducers on its own.

The administrator loader is tools/book/load-practice.R. It downloads pinned Eunomia datasets, verifies archive checksums and loads two SQLite files. From the book checkout, run Rscript tools/book/load-practice.R ../practice-data once in an R environment with DBI, RSQLite, openssl and jsonlite. The source data are Apache-2.0 licensed; keep their license with redistributed copies. The recorded loader results are in the reproduction notes.

Note

Chapters 5, 7, 9, 10 and 12–14 also use a tiny, separately labelled questionnaire test fixture for the colleague’s exact education, cause-of-death and partial-date examples. Its 24 fictional people and invented question concepts are not GiBleed or Synthea. It is created temporarily by tools/book/fixture.R, not installed as a third practice resource. Each chapter states its dataset.

Open the practice server

To reproduce without Opal, install the matching dsOMOP package and DSLite, DBI, RSQLite, resourcer, withr, dsBase and dsBaseClient. Open the book client directory as your R working directory. DSLite executes real DataSHIELD methods inside R; this helper creates one server with both loaded resources and attaches GiBleed.

source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- book_practice("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

conns holds connections, not patient rows. The other resource is named numeric. The numeric chapters start a fresh session with book_practice("numeric"). For a questionnaire-fixture chapter, source tools/book/fixture.R and use practice <- book_fixture(); conns <- practice$conns in a fresh R session.

Check the server 

ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....

The reply comes from the server. Check both the installed and published versions when using Opal: publishing makes the package methods available to analysts.

Use the same two resources on Opal

Requires a real Opal and an administrator. The recorded examples run on the two-resource DSLite practice server. For an Opal deployment, use the same loaded files and change the login/resource names; the study recipes stay the same.

  1. Install Docker with Compose V2 and start Docker. Install easy-opal with uv tool install easy-opal, or pipx install easy-opal.
  2. Run easy-opal setup; choose Opal, a local host, and a practice stack name. Run easy-opal up, then easy-opal status. Use the URL and credentials printed by setup. These steps follow the easy-opal guide.
  3. In Opal administration, select the Rock R profile used by DataSHIELD. Install dsBase and dsOMOP 2.10.4 in that profile and publish their DataSHIELD methods and options. A package installed only in your laptop’s R is not installed in Rock.
  4. Run Rscript tools/book/load-practice.R /data/practice on the practice host after installing the loader’s R dependencies. Mount that directory into Rock as /data/practice. The loaded gibleed.sqlite and numeric.sqlite files must be visible inside Rock, not merely inside the Opal container.
  5. In project practice, create the two resources below with format omop.dbi.db. SQLite needs no database username/password. Test each resource in Opal and grant the analyst use permission.
Opal resource Resource URL inside Rock Purpose
practice.gibleed omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/gibleed.sqlite Basics
practice.numeric omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/numeric.sqlite Numeric labs and units
  1. Log in with DSOpal as shown in chapter 2 and attach the resource named by the lesson. Keep these as database resources; do not import patient rows as a downloadable Opal table.

To move the practice setup to another Opal host, including a future opal-demo installation, transfer the same two files into its Rock mount and register those resource URLs there. No study-specific database TLS or privacy switch is required. The checksums and source revision make the data reproducible independently of where the resources are hosted.

Recap

You can distinguish your client installation from the server installation and have a practice connection.

Try it

Ask the client and server for their versions again. Which call needs a connection?

Solution

ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....
